name: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd.
business_summary: Hyderabad-based global generics, API (PSAI), biosimilar and branded-formulation company. Approximate mix (model knowledge, verify): North America ~38%, India ~27%, Emerging markets (Russia, CIS, Brazil etc.) ~17%, Europe ~10%, PSAI/API ~8%. Q2 FY27 sales Rs 8,698 cr (about -1.5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 1,723 cr (20%), PAT Rs 913-925 cr (-36% YoY) as gRevlimid (lenalidomide) fades and the Obeda semaglutide supply disruption hit; margin recovered from 5% (Mar-26 qtr) and 11% (Jun-26). Strategy: generic semaglutide (Canada, Brazil, India), abatacept/biosimilars. TTM sales Rs 33,097 cr; mcap Rs 1.14 lakh cr; borrowings rising (interest Rs 125 cr/qtr).

exposures.mechanism: US/N. America ~38% of sales (Rs ~3,300 cr/qtr). Base generics ex-gRevlimid ~65% of that; +5pp erosion = -3.3% US base -> -0.8% group sales; ~100% drop-through at 20% OPM = -4.1% EBITDA; EV/MCap 1.05, persistence 0.5 -> -2.2; add gRevlimid-cliff acceleration risk (lenalidomide full-generic competition, Q2 revenue already down on it) and semaglutide pricing competition -> -4.0. Management expects double-digit US growth ahead (CNBC TV18 2026-10-26), a counter-weight to downside.

evidence.note: DRL expects double-digit US growth; Q2 profit -36% on lower lenalidomide (CNBC TV18, Business Standard 2026-10-23)

exposures.mechanism: Generic semaglutide is the key near-term growth option: Canada generic injection (relaunch targeted for Nov 2026 after production disruption, scanx 2026-10-30), Brazil ANVISA approval 2026-11-05 (Business Standard), India oral Obeda tablets launched 2026-11-05 plus new generic Ozempic brands (Reuters 2026-10-23). If adoption +1 unit (faster uptake / extended exclusivity gaps): semaglutide sales ~Rs 1,500-2,500 cr/yr at ~45% margin -> EBITDA +10-15%; EV/MCap 1.05, persistence 0.5 -> +5; range wide because Q1 was a -ve surprise (supply disruption). No empirical series.

evidence.note: Brazil ANVISA approves Dr Reddy's generic semaglutide (Business Standard/Kalkine 2026-11-05)

exposures.mechanism: Three USFDA Form 483 observations at FTO-9 Visakhapatnam after pre-approval inspection (Oct 2026; Business Today, Medical Dialogues) -> gating for pending launches (likely semaglutide/biosimilar fill-finish; model assumption); history of 2023-24 Srikakulam/Bachupally warning letters. Probability of OAI/PAI delay ~25% x -12% equity (approval delays on ~Rs 1,000 cr launches, EBITDA -6%) -> -3.0 per 'stricter' unit.

evidence.note: USFDA completes PAI at FTO-9; 3 Form 483 observations (Business Today 2026-10-15; Equitypandit 2026-10-15)

exposures.mechanism: 100% US tariff on branded pharma since 2026-09-29, with India's speciality drugs exempt; generics outside scope (Business Standard 2026-09-29). DRL US ~38% of sales, made in India; if +10pp tariff applied to generics: net absorbed 50% -> -1.9% sales -> EBITDA -9%; prob 10% over 12m, EV/MCap 1.05 -> -0.8 weighted. Some semaglutide/biosimilar assets are 'specialty' - exempted so far.

evidence.note: India among 20 jurisdictions exempted from US speciality-drug tariff (Firstpost 2026-09-29)

exposures.mechanism: USD/EUR/RUB/BRL-linked sales ~73% of total; imported RM+royalties ~12% of sales: net USD-linked ~ 60% x 3% = +1.8% of sales at 20% OPM = +9% EBITDA; hedges cover ~50% for 6-12m -> +4.5%; EV/MCap 1.05, persistence 0.5 -> +2.4; with EM currency pass-through uncertainty -> +3.2. Empirical +1.73 (t=1.4) lower; rupee has strengthened 1.9% in 1m, a headwind to the Q3 print.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 20.6% (Goodreturns 2026-10-23); INR 94.49, -1.9% in 1m

exposures.mechanism: China-origin KSMs/intermediates are a notable part of PSAI inputs (model knowledge ~20% of RM); +15% Chinese price cuts reduce RM ~3% and compress PSAI selling prices too; net small positive for formulations (RM ~32% of costs -> -1% cost = +5% EBITDA at 20% OPM, half competed away) -> +0.8.

evidence.note: PSAI is ~8% of sales; margin recovery to 20% is the stated FY27 target (Sahi 2026-09-29)

exposures.mechanism: Borrowings have risen (interest Rs 125 cr/qtr vs Rs 83 cr a year ago; annual Rs 450 cr TTM vs EBITDA Rs 4,853 cr). ~Rs 7,000 cr of debt (estimate), 50% floating: +25bp = Rs 9 cr/yr = 0.2% of EBITDA, negligible; discount-rate effect on a 40x TTM P/E -> -0.8.

Russia/CIS ~10% of sales and Gulf/EM logistics; escalation lifts freight & solvents (~0.5% of costs) -> EBITDA -2.5%, persistence 0.25 -> -0.7. Empirical Brent +0.79 (t=1.8) is positive (Brent up, rupee down, oil-linked market rotation) so model sign kept low-weight.

India 27% of sales, branded Rx and consumer health (Nicotex/ Haleon NRT), 12% weight of incremental discretionary -> +5pp urban lifts India sales 1pp = +0.27% group sales; +1.4% EBITDA; EV/MCap 1.05, persistence 0.5 -> +0.7.
FII holding down to 20.3% from 21.1% in Mar 2026 but DIIs up; large-cap defensive with beta 0.62. +US$5bn FPI quarterly inflow -> +0.6 beyond beta.

supply_chain.note: semaglutide patent expiry in Canada/Brazil/India opens generic window; patent/litigation risk

supply_chain.counterparty: US wholesaler buying groups (McKesson, Cardinal, Cencora)
Cipla, Sun, Lupin, Zydus, Teva (US generics)

Q3 FY27 results: US growth, semaglutide Canada/Brazil/India revenue, EBITDA toward ~20% FY27 target
USFDA closure/classification of FTO-9 Visakhapatnam PAI
Abatacept biosimilar filing/approval milestones (CFO flagged as next growth phase)
